_meta.purpose: The business map: architecture / strategy / product / decisions / goals / constraints judged out of the four legacy graphs (2026-11-19) and re-filed into the clean graph live-v5 (org 3326a01ea34ae595d84de5d8f9, graph g_311d79c684de4d0e8953d189ed) through the normal doors.
_meta.law: docs/ONTOLOGY.md v3.38 core + packs/product-strategy + packs/venture. A decision is an Event (eventKind: decision); a goal is an Object (goalState); a person/role is a Subject (subjectKind + holdsRole, distinct from memberOf); a document/url is a Source; a claim is a Point (pointKind: statement); support/contradiction between epistemic nodes is an operator (IMPL/NAND).
_meta.provenance: Every item names the legacy carrier it was judged from in `legacy`. Items whose authority is a repo document name it in `source` (filed as a :Source, and wired with `extractedFrom` where the claim came from the document). Nothing here is a copy of a legacy node: every item was re-judged and re-stated.
_meta.dropped_categories: See JUDGEMENT.md — PR-review chatter, CI/test minutiae, harness/lane ops, GraphEvent journal, Session/onboarding bookkeeping, synthetic benchmark corpora, and duplicates.
_meta.idempotency: Subjects merge by name; Objects merge by name; Points are created with dedup=true; edges are checked before creation. Re-running any batch is safe.

objects.name: Tortoise
objects.why: The marketable offering: a semantic / epistemic / episodic memory graph for agents (SDK + MCP server + hosted API).

objects.name: the agent-memory market
objects.why: The competitive arena the product operates in; eight systems were surveyed in the legacy corpus.

objects.name: Graphiti
objects.why: Named competitor in the legacy survey and in product/competition/.

objects.name: Neo4j Agent Memory
objects.why: Named competitor in the legacy survey.

objects.name: GraphRAG
objects.why: Named competitor in the legacy survey.

objects.name: Supermemory
objects.why: Named competitor; also present in product/competition/supermemory.md.

objects.name: Letta / Cognee
objects.why: Named competitor (product/competition/letta-cognee.md); the ecosystem the buyer compares against.

objects.name: validate revenue
objects.why: Top goal of the beta cascade: prove someone pays for Tortoise. Owner-stated 2026-11-02. No pass/fail metric declared yet.

objects.name: launch private beta
objects.why: Owner-stated goal; the beta launch is how revenue gets validated. Blocked 2026-11-02 because neither gate was met.

objects.name: merge all P0 and P1 issues
objects.why: Gate 1 for the private beta. Measured 2026-11-02: 15 P0-blocker + 28 P1-severe open; 0 closed by a merge in the hour to 15:25Z.

objects.name: announcement ready for the interested segment in Attio CRM
objects.why: Gate 2 for the private beta. The owner defined 'interested' as an Attio pipeline stage; the count was UNEVALUATED at 16:25Z.

objects.name: reduce agent-harness bottlenecks
objects.why: Subgoal of Gate 1 (owner correction 2026-11-02: NOT of the announcement gate).

objects.name: C1: venv reaping matches a bare relative argv
objects.why: Throughput unblocker named by the owner: the reaper never matched a bare relative .venv/bin/python argv.

objects.name: C2: the merge rail exits instead of waiting forever
objects.why: A stuck merge must not hold a merge slot for hours.

objects.name: C3: every queued CI run is attributed to a cause
objects.why: The queue must be diagnosable rather than a number.

objects.name: C4: deployed code equals the pin
objects.why: Every box runs the pinned tree, so a fix that landed is a fix that is live.

objects.name: C5: review throughput
objects.why: A required per-PR review check makes review capacity a hard ceiling on merges per hour.

objects.name: a16z Speedrun SR008
objects.why: Highest-priority funding programme in the legacy accelerator survey; window Oct 12 - Nov 1, up to $1M as $500K / 10% SAFE + $500K next round, cohort late Jan - Apr 2027.

objects.name: YC W2027
objects.why: Second priority; deadline Nov 2 8pm PT, decision Dec 11 (single-source in the corpus).

objects.name: ERA W'27
objects.why: Same-day fallback in the priority sequence; shares the November deadline cluster.

objects.name: Techstars Spring 2027
objects.why: November deadline cluster; the London deal terms ($220K for 5%) are single-sourced in the corpus.

objects.name: EF The Bridge cycle
objects.why: Named in the same funding programme table.

objects.name: HF0
objects.why: Part of the top-tier accelerator cluster the survey judged dense enough to make the ruled-out programmes cost no viable path.

objects.name: no per-graph caps and no node-count pricing
objects.why: Standing pricing constraint: nodes were retired as the customer-facing unit; free=1 graph, solo=2, pro/team unlimited; storage is the purchasable dimension and it is per account.

objects.name: the MCP and SDK surface cannot grow by accident
objects.why: Adding or removing a tool from TOOL_REGISTRY or a public method on TortoiseSDK needs the owner's approval first; the surface manifest is the drift control, not the approval.

objects.name: no capture caps
objects.why: Owner ruling #4010 on the capture path.

objects.name: the record is truth and the graph is a derived hot cache
objects.why: STORAGE-ARCHITECTURE §2.0: Postgres is the system of record, the graph is a projection that must be re-derivable.

events.content: The private-beta launch was held blocked on 2026-11-02 by measurement, not by opinion: 15 P0-blocker and 28-29 P1-severe issues were open and no P0/P1 had been closed by a merge in the hour to 15:25Z. The owner named the two gates (merge all P0/P1; announcement ready for the 'interested' Attio population) as the only paths to the launch.
events.legacy: core:goal objects 'launch private beta' / 'merge all P0 and P1 issues' / 'announcement ready ... Attio CRM' with their summaries and evidence fields; decision events 'The owner corrected the goal cascade: reduce bottlenecks is a subgoal of GATE-B1'

events.content: The owner defined 'interested' for the beta announcement as a PIPELINE STAGE in the Attio CRM, so the gate population is every prospect whose Attio opportunity sits at that stage. The stage count was not measurable from the box on 2026-11-02, which is what kept the gate at active rather than met.
events.legacy: core:goal 'announcement ready for the interested segment in Attio CRM' summary; goal-cascade lane

events.content: Owner decision (Gate #2): pro and team have unlimited graphs, free keeps 1 and solo 2, and NO pricing value changes when per-graph tenancy ships. The per-graph key and recording features ship without becoming per-graph charges.
events.legacy: product/pricing.json _comment (Epic #2083, Gate #2) as corroborated by the legacy pricing findings

events.content: Owner ruling (#11758): the two purchasable storage dimensions are stored data (Postgres bytes) and hot capacity (graph MB); the allowance and the bill are PER ACCOUNT, so a second graph does not double the allowance and adds no second line.

Nodes were retired as the customer-facing pricing unit (#4495/#5331): the node cap was replaced, not extended. A capability census therefore cannot contradict the recorded decision of no per-graph caps, no node-count pricing, and unlimited graphs per tenant.
events.legacy: point 'The capability census PR does not contradict the recorded decision of no per-graph caps, no node-count pricing, and unlimited graphs per tenant.'

events.content: The owner ruled that the fleet's memory is the Tortoise hosted graph, and that every dispatch uses the research skill, which must check the graph before deriving.
events.legacy: decision event 'The owner ruled on 2026-11-02 that the fleet's memory is the Tortoise hosted graph ...'

events.content: Owner ruling 2026-11-01T05:58Z postponed the entire hosted deployment setup and named the arming issue explicitly: do not arm, provision, or point anything at the hosted store until it is settled.
events.legacy: decision event 'The owner ruling of 2026-11-01T05:58Z postponed the entire hosted deployment setup ...'

events.content: Owner ruling under EXTRACTOR-V4 §S3: phase 2 of the extractor is committed to RECEIVING the S1 narrative rather than re-deriving it. The narrative is the load-bearing artifact; later phases consume it.

events.content: The owner approved the v3.37 ontology status-model change and the lifecycle vocabulary ('good > easy': the structurally correct fix rather than the smallest diff). Six hunks plus a version bump to the ontology standard were approved on 2026-11-17: one closed set of four statuses for every knowledge kind, with retracted/outdated/archived demoted to read-side legacy.
events.legacy: decision events 'The v3.37 ontology status-model change was approved by the owner as good > easy', 'The owner approved the exact text of the ONTOLOGY.md lifecycle-vocabulary change on 2026-11-17'

events.content: The owner ruled that 'stop sending graph on writes' is not a candidate fix but a REOPENING of the graph-as-tool-argument decision, and must reopen that decision rather than ship quietly. The same rule was applied to the default-graph form on 2026-10-27.
events.legacy: decision events 'The owner ruled on the graph-omission P0 that stop sending graph on writes is not a candidate but a reopening of the graph-as-tool-argument decision' and 'The owner ruled on 2026-10-27 that the default-graph form is the pre-#9340 defect ...'

events.content: The owner ruled that measurement tools be described generically in user-facing text, retiring vendor and cookie names from what a customer reads.
events.legacy: decision event 'The owner ruled on 2026-11-15 that measurement tools be described generically, retiring vendor and cookie names from the user-facing text'

events.content: The owner ruled the shape of the business map itself: do not bloat the ontology — packs plus core already declare the business logic, so this is a business-mapping exercise. Notes about a PR going through review are noise; what is wanted is architecture, strategy, product. A superseded duplicate carries no knowledge of its own.

Owner ruling #4010 on the capture path: no capture caps. Extraction is not rationed by a cap on how much of a session is captured — a cap there decides what the product may know, which is a product decision the owner keeps.
events.legacy: issue #4010 as cited by every lane brief ('No capture caps (#4010)') and the standard 'no capture caps' object

events.content: The Wave-1 exit gate was replaced: the 'aha test' is WITHDRAWN as the gate and as open owner decision #1, and the gate is now the nine objectives' done-states, each observed against the running system. The 2026-09-22 plan supersedes-in-part the 2026-09-17 plan and the 2026-09-13 roadmap, which still carry the old aha gate and must be read as superseded rather than authoritative.
events.legacy: points attached to the legacy Objects 'Tortoise beta roadmap' and 'Tortoise beta plan' in org_3326a01ea34ae595d84de5d8f9 ('The aha test is withdrawn as the Wave-1 exit gate ... the gate is now the nine objectives' done-states'; '... explicitly supersedes_in_part the 2026-09-17 plan and 2026-09-13 roadmap')

points.content: Postgres is the system of record and the graph is a derived hot cache: every graph node must be re-derivable from the journal, so a node written only to the graph is the defect, not the optimization.
points.legacy: docs/architecture/STORAGE-ARCHITECTURE.md §2.0 as carried by the legacy 'record is truth' findings and the GraphEvent journal (76,610 nodes of the largest legacy graph) that exists to make replay possible

points.content: GraphEvent, Session, Meta, EpMeta and the onboarding nodes are the write-ahead journal and capture bookkeeping, not knowledge: 76,610 GraphEvent nodes of the largest legacy graph's 126,908 nodes (60% of them — the census in JUDGEMENT.md §3, measured 2026-11-19). Their home is the record, and re-filing them into a belief graph would duplicate the journal into the cache.
points.legacy: label census of the four legacy graphs; issue #13880 source table

points.content: A decision is an Event on the timeline, not a first-class Point: the graph says 'this state is based on these reasons', never 'this decision was made because of these reasons'. Filing a decision as a Point is a kind error.
points.legacy: docs/ONTOLOGY.md §2 state-centric model and §5 point-kind vocabulary; re-derived from #13420

points.content: A goal is an Object carrying goalState (met / active / blocked / unmet / superseded / abandoned), which is a different axis from status: status says whether the goal is promoted for use, goalState says whether it is met.
points.legacy: core:goal objects with goalState; ontology §4.1/§5 (#7856)

points.content: A person holding a role is not membership: holdsRole (person to role) is a distinct predicate from memberOf (member to team or org), and collapsing the two loses who is accountable for what.
points.legacy: docs/ONTOLOGY.md §3.6 note on holdsRole vs memberOf

points.content: A document is a Source, not an Object: its bytes live outside the graph, and the claims extracted from it carry the epistemic weight while extractedFrom ties each claim back to where it was read.
points.legacy: docs/ONTOLOGY.md §4.4/§4.6; legacy corpus shape (3,035 Sources, 16,185 extractedFrom edges)

points.content: The public SDK surface is being consolidated from 91 tools/methods toward 27: the surface is a contract every integration is built on, so it may not grow by accident and every retirement must name a customer-visible replacement.
points.legacy: core:target 'tortoise SDK 91->27 tool consolidation target'; point 'The 66 retirement records exist mechanically in RETIRED_SDK_METHODS but name no replacement'

points.content: Every one of the eight agent-memory systems surveyed has effectively one write door — a single write entry point.
points.legacy: points attached to Graphiti / Neo4j Agent Memory / GraphRAG in team_7a3b5403935f865c27d3fb1751

points.content: Graphiti exposes three write APIs — add_episode, add_episode_bulk, add_triplet — so it does not have a single write entry point.
points.legacy: point attached to competitor Graphiti

points.content: Neo4j Agent Memory documents batch, streaming and buffered writes alongside its MemoryClient, so it too has more than one write entry point.
points.legacy: point attached to competitor Neo4j Agent Memory

points.content: GraphRAG is a batch pipeline with an update path rather than a single write entry point, and its documented update command offers standard and fast incremental indexing — so 'full re-index is the norm' is not a safe claim.
points.legacy: points attached to competitor GraphRAG

points.content: Supermemory has no as-of / time-travel search capability: it cannot answer what the memory held at a past instant.
points.legacy: point attached to competitor Supermemory

points.content: Four top-priority funding programmes (Speedrun SR008, YC W2027, ERA W'27, Techstars Spring 2027) share overlapping November deadlines and all require a US entity — so the deadline cluster is a single constraint, not four independent choices.
points.legacy: point attached to YC W2027 in team_7a3b5403935f865c27d3fb1751

points.content: The funding priority sequence is a16z Speedrun SR008 first (window Oct 12 - Nov 1, up to $1M as $500K / 10% SAFE plus $500K in the next round, cohort late Jan - Apr 2027), then YC W2027 (Nov 2, decision Dec 11), with ERA as the same-day fallback and Techstars on Nov 18.
points.legacy: point attached to a16z Speedrun

points.content: The top-tier accelerator cluster (Speedrun, YC, ERA, Techstars, HF0) is dense enough that the ruled-out programmes (Hello Tomorrow, 4YFN, SXSW Pitch, MuckerLab) cost no viable path.
points.legacy: point attached to YC W2027

points.content: SXSW Pitch is ruled out for 2027 because it requires the product to have launched before 1 January 2024, which an alpha fails conditional on incorporation.
points.legacy: point attached to SXSW Pitch (product-strategy:campaign) in team_7a3b5403935f865c27d3fb1751

points.content: Two funding terms in the survey are single-sourced and must be verified before a decision rests on them: Techstars' standard deal ($220K for 5%) has no inline source, and Y Combinator's W2027 deadline carries no ycombinator.com citation.
points.legacy: points attached to Techstars London and YC W2027

points.content: At 1,000,000 MAU Supabase's total ($2,925) is the lowest of any provider that meters MAU — the unit-economics floor the hosted product is measured against.
points.legacy: point attached to customerSegment 'MAU-metered providers'

points.content: Identity Platform's per-unit rate falls to $0.0032 in the 1M-10M band, so auth cost is not linear in MAU at the top of the band.
points.legacy: point attached to competitor 'Identity Platform' (an auth vendor in the legacy cost comparison)

points.content: The same DeepSeek model carries a wide price spread by supplier: v4-flash is $0.07/$0.14 per 1M tokens on OpenRouter against $0.138/$0.275 on Venice, and v4-pro-0813 is ~$0.579/$1.738 on OpenRouter against $1.65/$4.95 on Venice. Supplier choice for the extraction leg is a real cost lever, not a rounding error.
points.legacy: points attached to deepseek-v4-flash-0731 / deepseek-v4-pro-0813 in team_7a3b5403935f865c27d3fb1751

points.content: Every paid tier includes an amount of stored data and hot capacity and buys more above it at the published rate, while free and anon publish no included record amount and are REFUSED at their included amount instead: an over-cap write on a paid tier is a bill, on free it is a refusal.
points.legacy: product/pricing.json storage block (#11758); legacy point 'D11 - over-cap refused, under-cap succeeds'

points.content: The 2026-11-02 gate measurement is the baseline the beta launch is judged against: 15 P0-blocker plus 28-29 P1-severe open, and one PR merged in the hour to 15:25Z that closed no P1.
points.legacy: core:goal 'merge all P0 and P1 issues' summary/evidence

points.content: No revenue metric and no measurement of revenue validation existed at 2026-11-02, which is why 'validate revenue' sits at goalState=active: achievement could not be evidenced either way.
points.legacy: core:goal 'GOAL-A: validate revenue' evidence field

points.content: When two lanes carry the same commitment, the earlier carrier wins and the later one is superseded naming the winner: a duplicate is retired with a supersedeReason, never left live beside its twin.
points.legacy: core:goal 'GOAL-A: validate revenue' supersededBy/supersedeReason

points.content: The agent-harness throughput work is a CONSTRAINT on the product's roadmap, not a product goal in its own right: it exists because merging P0/P1 is gated on the pipeline moving at all.
points.legacy: core:goal 'reduce agent-harness bottlenecks' summary; owner correction of the cascade

points.content: A deletion of raw content is an ACT, recorded durably and bounded by a 10-day deletion-marker TTL, and a recorded act always wins over a live observation: a probe can never un-delete a memory.
points.legacy: docs/retention-and-deletion.md as cited by the Source rawState axis; legacy 'retention-doctrine quote' point

points.content: The beta's Wave-1 exit criterion is not a statistic: it is the nine objectives' done-states, each observed against the running system. A gate phrased as a cohort size plus a success bar was withdrawn precisely because it could not be observed against the system.
points.legacy: 'Tortoise beta roadmap' claims: 'The roadmap still asserts that the value scorecard's statistics depend on the cohort numbers in open decision 1, contradicting the withdrawal' + the withdrawal itself
